sections.h2: What does a Goldsboro owner choose between when selling?
sections.html:
Goldsboro owners weigh a listing against a private sale or a cash offer, and repairs, timing and what you owe settle the choice. Goldsboro is the Wayne County seat, so deeds, tax questions and estate filings all lead to offices in the city.

  • Listing: more buyers, more preparation.
  • Private sale: no agent fee, more of the paperwork on you.
  • Cash offer: fewer steps and a closing date you pick, generally under a retail price.

Whichever way you go, get the buyer's terms in writing and let a closing attorney read them.

sections.h2: What shapes the Goldsboro housing market?
sections.html:
Goldsboro sits in eastern North Carolina on US 70, within about 30 minutes of the I-40 and I-95 corridors, according to the city's website. It became the Wayne County seat in 1847 and the name changed from Goldsborough to Goldsboro in 1869.

The city grew where the Wilmington and Raleigh railroad crossed the New Bern Road, and it now covers more than 25 square miles. Seymour Johnson Air Force Base, home of the 4th Fighter Wing and the 916th Air Refueling Wing, sits on the southeast side of the city.

The county's general information page puts the base's civilian and military payroll above $407 million and its fiscal year 2021 economic impact above $727 million. Military moves tend to come in cycles, so owners who rent to base families should plan for turnover when a lease ends.

sections.h2: What do I know about Wayne County's land and farm economy?
sections.html:
Wayne County is level to gently rolling land with the Neuse River crossing its lower central part. The county says elevations are mostly 120 to 145 feet above sea level and the growing season runs about 225 days.

Farming and manufacturing both matter locally. The county lists products from bread and poultry feed to automobile parts and electric transformers, and swine was the largest source of farm income in the 2006 data on that page.

For a seller, the Neuse River and nearby creeks mean it is worth asking about flood zone status, since a lender or buyer may require it. Ask the Wayne County tax or planning office, or your insurance agent, for the status of your parcel.

sections.h2: What tax dates apply to a Goldsboro house?
sections.html:
Wayne County bills real property tax once a year, and the city adds its own tax on the same bill cycle under the state calendar. Bills fall due September 1, and the state treats payment before January 6 as on time.

Ask the Wayne County Tax Office for your parcel's value, the current rates and the date of the county's next revaluation, because those figures are set locally.

sections.h2: What if I owe back property tax on a Goldsboro house?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax is a lien on the parcel, and the county can enforce it by foreclosure. G.S. 105-355 says the lien attaches as of the date property is to be listed, with penalties, interest and costs attached at the same time.

Under G.S. 105-374 the foreclosure is conducted like a mortgage foreclosure, with a public sale at the courthouse door to the highest bidder. The commissioner may ask for a deposit up to 20 percent of the bid, and exceptions or an increased bid may be filed within 10 days after the sale report.

Before the court confirms the sale, the owner can redeem by paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Selling the house first and paying the tax at closing is another way out, so ask the tax office for a payoff figure.

sections.h2: What should I know if I sold or bought under a contract for deed?
sections.html:
Contract for deed deals in North Carolina fall under Chapter 47H, and the statute gives buyers several protections. It covers agreements with five or more payments, where the seller keeps title, for homes of one to four families priced at $5,000 or more.

  • The contract must be written, signed and acknowledged.
  • The buyer may cancel until midnight of the third business day after signing or delivery.
  • The seller must record the contract or a memorandum within five business days.
  • A forfeiture needs written notice with a cure date at least 30 days after service.

If you hold a contract for deed on a Goldsboro house and want to sell, have an attorney confirm the notice steps before you act.

sections.h2: What about tenants when a Goldsboro house is sold in foreclosure?
sections.html:
Tenants in a residence of fewer than 15 rental units get a right to end the lease after a foreclosure sale. G.S. 45-21.16A says tenants under rental agreements made or renewed on or after October 1, 2007 may terminate on at least 10 but no more than 90 days' notice after the sale date.

If you rent your Goldsboro house to base families or others and a sale is coming, tell the tenant early and put the date in writing. Eviction for a non-paying tenant goes through small claims before a magistrate, and the state court page lists the fee as $96 with sheriff service at $30.

sections.h2: How do I keep the costs of a Goldsboro sale clear?
sections.html:
Ask each buyer for a written net sheet showing price, taxes, payoff and fees. Your attorney can confirm the total before you sign.

City Hall sits downtown at 200 North Center Street and is open 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays, according to the city's website. The city says its recent projects include the Center Street Streetscape work and the Bryan Multi-Sports Complex, and it employs 484 full-time staff.

Cash Home Buyers makes offers on Goldsboro houses in any condition, including inherited homes and rentals. Compare that figure with the net from a listing and decide with all the numbers in front of you.

faqs.q: Is Goldsboro the Wayne County seat?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's website says Goldsboro became the Wayne County seat in 1847.

faqs.q: Where does a Goldsboro deed get recorded?
faqs.a: At the Wayne County register of deeds, which collects the excise tax before it records the instrument.

faqs.q: What is the state's deed excise rate?
faqs.a: The statute prints $1.00 on each $500 or fractional part of the value conveyed.

faqs.q: Can unpaid county tax force a sale of my Goldsboro house?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien can be enforced by foreclosure under G.S. 105-374, and the owner can redeem before confirmation by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

faqs.q: What notice must a contract for deed forfeiture give?
faqs.a: Written notice of default with a cure date at least 30 days after service, per Chapter 47H.
